human_tolerance.notes: Common in urban parks as well as deciduous woodland, and readily settles where rocky areas, brush or log piles and shrubs give cover; it carries food in its cheek pouches and lines its burrows with leaves, rocks and sticks.

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: During the winter the chipmunk may enter long periods of hibernation, relying on the food stores carried into its burrow in the cheek pouches.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: First of the two breeding seasons; a female usually produces one or two litters of three to five young, which stay with the mother for about six to eight weeks.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Second of the two breeding seasons, June to August.

phases.name: moult
phases.note: Molt occurs once or twice annually, during May or June and sometimes again in October.

vocalizations.description: One of a repertoire of five stereotyped sounds, the chip, used in alarm and in keeping contact; the whole repertoire is the chip, the chuck, the trills, the whistle or squeal, and chatter.
A trill measured at 130 trills per minute, given in daylight while foraging, when the animal is most active.
Chatter, given when a chipmunk is disturbed at its burrow, which it defends against anything that intrudes.

range.note: Lives in deciduous wooded areas and urban parks throughout the eastern United States and southern Canada.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Wikipedia describes foraging on the ground for most of the day, climbing trees well, and moving with a fast run; walk and trot are the mapping of that, and Climb is the documented tree climbing.

traits.nest_type.note: It constructs underground nests with extensive tunnel systems and often several entrances, lining the burrows with leaves, rocks, sticks and other material.

traits.perching.note: Set to false: it climbs trees but is described as a ground forager that shelters in a burrow, not a perching animal.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 66-150 g weight range.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia's stated length of about 30 cm including the tail.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'On average, eastern chipmunks live three or more years in the wild, but in captivity they may live as long as eight years.'

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia lists bulbs, seeds, fruits, nuts, green plants, mushrooms, insects, worms and bird eggs, and records that food is commonly transported in cheek pouches. No open source gives percentages, so the 40/20/15/15/10 split across seed, browse, invertebrate, fruit and mast is authored judgement within the described list; bird eggs and mushrooms are omitted as trace items.

traits.social.note: 'The eastern chipmunk defends its burrow and lives a solitary life, except during mating season'; the upper bound of 2 covers a mother with pups.

traits.activity_pattern.note: 'The chipmunk is mainly active during the day, spending most of its day foraging', with winter hibernation.

traits.defense.note: It defends its burrow and flees to it, with a large predator list including hawks, owls, foxes, raccoons, snakes and cats; Flee is the judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: bold in parks and gardens and quick to approach, but it dives into its burrow at any sudden movement.

habitat.use.note: The ground share follows Wikipedia's account of a mainly ground-foraging animal that constructs underground nests; the arboreal share covers the tree climbing it is documented to do well.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the log_pile entry follows Wikipedia's statement that it prefers rocky areas, brush or log piles and shrubs for cover, recorded here as a landscape resource rather than a food type; burrow weight is from the extensive tunnel systems it constructs.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia records the species in urban parks as well as deciduous wooded areas and gives its preference for rocky areas, brush or log piles and shrubs as cover; it does not describe bird-feeder or garden use, so those are not claimed here.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'During the winter, the chipmunk may enter long periods of hibernation.'

seasonal.triggers.note: Authored judgement. Wikipedia says only that 'during the winter, the chipmunk may enter long periods of hibernation' and gives no temperature or photoperiod threshold, day length is used as the proxy: enter after 90 days below 10 hours of daylight, which at northern-US latitudes spans the core of the winter, and leave after 30 days above 11 hours.

seasonal.phases.note: The two breeding seasons (February to April, June to August), litter size, the six-to-eight-week period with the mother, winter hibernation and the May-June (sometimes October) molt are all stated in Wikipedia.

seasonal.life_stages.note: The duration follows Wikipedia's statement that pups spend around six to eight weeks with their mothers; the scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.note: Wikipedia quotes a five-sound repertoire - the chip, the chuck, the trills, the whistle or squeal, and chatter - and gives the trill rate of 130 per minute. The assignment of chip and chatter to Alarm and trill to Contact is authored judgement, since the article does not label the contexts; the cooldowns are authored judgement.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description of reddish-brown fur on the upper body, five dark brown stripes contrasting with light brown stripes along the back, and a dark tail; the light belly is the standard chipmunk countershading and is judgement. The stripe, cheek-pouch and tail parts and the proportions are authored judgement to render the stripes and the pouches the description names.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program. food_tag is 'seed' because seeds and bulbs head the diet and it spends most of the day foraging on the ground; the sun band is set to -90/-6 for a diurnal species, so it rests in its burrow at night; flee_gait is a trot for its fast run. All radii are judgement.
